The net only ever saw train_n=200 = 35% of the 579-slice train pool (3 ps-groups: 154@0.66192 / 98@0.73979 / 327@0.77873). (3) ONE KNOB: train_n 200 -> 480 (35% -> 83% train-pool coverage). I REVERT to the iter-1 BEST config (wu_n_bands=4, wu_n_outer=1, lr0.01) -- NOT the regressed iter-3/4 -- and change ONLY train_n, mirroring the confirmed uswin/itnet_v3 recipe (revert-to-best, then raise coverage). It does NOT use RotatingSubsetDataset, so train_n IS load-bearing data coverage, not inert. (4) HYPOTHESIS: if wu_2015_trainable hr-0.05 ceiling is data-coverage-limited (only 35% of the train pool seen), raising train_n 200->480 lifts hr measurably above the iter-1 best 0.0508 (SSIM > 0.842, >+0.005 over the +-0.001 noise band). NUMERIC FALSIFIER (terminal): if hr <= 0.051 (at/below iter-1 best) at train_n=480, the ceiling is the FBP-family architecture itself (band-reweighted FBP + soft-thresholded residual, NO image-domain learned CNN denoiser), not data coverage -- file the terminal verdict (epochs, bands, outer-depth AND data all exhausted; caps hr~0.05 on real-helical Mayo, far below dual-domain U-Net families hr~0.27). (5) BUDGET (HARD 1200s/20-min train+score): iter-1 335s at train_n=200/ep6/n_outer=1 = 1200 train-slice-passes + a fixed 214-slice val pass. To hold the wall AND keep grad-step parity (train_n x epochs ~ 200x6=1200), I trade epochs 6->3: 480x3=1440 train-slice-passes (+20% vs iter-1). Worst-case linear scaling ~335x1.2 ~= 400s train+score, well under 1200s and the 1800s SLURM kill; val FIGURE outside budget. ep3 is safe AND a non-regression on the optimization axis because iter-2 PROVED epochs inert (ep6==ep18) -- this isolates train_n as the SOLE meaningful change. n_outer held at 1 (MANDATORY hint; also keeps the dominant 2x-dense residual pass single).
